disclosure: A local static copy of two independently authored public research indexes. Relevance is about documents and proposed experiments, not real available helpers, partners, services, verified acts, permission, or human identity. Links are unverified until opened.

sources.disclosure: This curated, dated catalog is not a live availability feed, service enrollment, or verified community roster. Source commits identify public project text; they do not establish partnerships, permission, field completion or canonical adoption. Every community and project retains its own authority.

Manually curated organizational plan pointers. planZ does not own local projects. Issue links show a plan exists, not that programs, partners or field acts are approved, funded or completed. This public map contains no resident, donor, contact or shelter-site records.

entries.title: Jubilee Circuit — The Road Brings the Feast
entries.summary: A published music-first field kit connects voluntary festival, church and community gathering ideas to locally approved useful work. Ghana and Minnesota are candidate sites, not enrolled partners.
entries.reviewQuestion: Can one willing host and independent local steward review a two-hour gathering and a consented song seed?

entries.title: Porchlight Commons — Minnesota ↔ Ghana
entries.summary: An organizational HOLD-card desk compares local procurement, remote donations and knowledge transfer for community-selected food, power and communication needs. No live matching, shipping or provider enrollment.
entries.reviewQuestion: Which organization-level need would a locally authorized receiving steward choose to describe?

entries.title: The Garden — community food access and federation
entries.summary: Waseca food-access and producer-direct ideas explore a locally governed grocery, pilot shelves, grower connections and reusable intercommunity learning. No cooperative or venue consent is implied.
entries.reviewQuestion: What decision or small practical test do the independent grocery organizers actually want help reviewing?

entries.title: Night Desk — useful work after dark
entries.summary: A public night-work desk explores bounded tasks, stewardship and distinct stages from proposed help to independently reviewed results. A web page is not an emergency dispatch or verified service.
entries.reviewQuestion: What safe, reversible task can someone prepare or review tonight without unapproved access to people or sites?

entries.title: reLATTE COMMUTER — farm and cooperative communication
entries.summary: A tested library prototype expresses source change → signed crossing → receiver-owned HOLD/ADMIT/REFUSE → idempotent destination action. It is not connected to a real farm, email account or live worker.
entries.reviewQuestion: What source system, receiver permission and destination adapter could an operator safely test with synthetic records?

entries.title: Weaves → we'ves — work that inherits
entries.summary: The local JAR;VIS operator notebook separates a possible task, voluntary stated commitment, reported result, separate review and reusable candidate method. This is not public verified fulfillment.
entries.reviewQuestion: Can a small task yield a recorded report and independent review without assuming the participant is authenticated?

entries.title: Reviewer discovery and voluntary stewardship
entries.summary: An owner-approved experimental reviewer role portal supports private opt-in interest and operator screening. A role application is not verified identity, independent review or appointment.
entries.reviewQuestion: Which question requires a reviewer, and who may independently approve that person's scope?

entries.title: Still Here — survivor-led practical support
entries.summary: A survivor-first front-door and voluntary stewardship concept preserves privacy, safeguarding and the right to start with a small task. It is not an active referral, peer matching or crisis service.
entries.reviewQuestion: What safeguarding and responsible-human review must exist before inviting vulnerable people into a shared service?

entries.title: Static Live and the listening room
entries.summary: Static Live describes consented performance packets, stage projections and attributable music; the public listening room carries songs and letters. Neither implies permission to reuse anyone else's recording.
entries.reviewQuestion: Which artist or community voluntarily licenses a song seed and chooses how replies may be recorded, credited or shared?

entries.title: Coalition of Care and provider-first practical assistance
entries.summary: A provider-first homelessness response on-ramp proposes a small, authorized neighbor-help task with an independent lived-experience reviewer. This is not an official coalition program or provider service.
entries.reviewQuestion: Which existing provider would review one task without transferring private client records or case management?

entries.title: Abundent Switchboard — public doors
entries.summary: The Abundent Switchboard lists independent experiments and marks preview or repair status separately. A link is a door, not shared governance or a promise of operational service.
entries.reviewQuestion: Which existing working door serves the particular question, and is its public hostname actually reachable?

entries.title: Becoming — organizations that don't exist yet
entries.summary: A public open-chair identity for emerging organizations and ideas; it does not invent staff, legal status, founding history or partner approvals.
entries.reviewQuestion: What concrete first invitation would let another person voluntarily help shape an unformed organization?

entries.title: LemonPRESS — print, digital and local publication
entries.summary: LemonPRESS separates physical, digital, crawler and archive editions. A low-cost community newspaper, newsletters and local distribution are ideas to test; no publication partner or printed issue is assumed.
entries.reviewQuestion: Which local publisher or printer would review one consented, inexpensive pilot page and distribution route?

entries.title: Post Office — owned email and consented correspondence
entries.summary: An owner-authorized outbound Resend self-test reached provider acceptance, not independently confirmed inbox delivery. Community newsletters and opt-in outreach require verified consent, suppression and delivery checks.
entries.reviewQuestion: Can the owner verify inbox receipt and replies before adding a consented newsletter or invitation list?

entries.title: planZ — public plan blockers and next human gates
entries.summary: planZ now publishes a tested, hand-reviewed, seven-plan organizational attention index; JAR;VIS's localhost workbench can explicitly inspect it and surface topical blockers. It is a subset, not the global census or a live executor.
entries.reviewQuestion: Which owner-source issue and outstanding local permission must be reviewed before one plan can proceed?

entries.title: Between Rooms — the institutional proposal is the first bridge
entries.summary: A public, source-backed interactive proposal maps nine prospective institutional doors onto one fictional food-access problem, with institution-specific drafts, local simulated HOLD/REFUSE and portable JSON. None of the institutions is a partner, invited participant or verified recipient.
entries.reviewQuestion: Which one authorized local steward, actual non-sensitive problem and one recipient door should be human-reviewed before any outreach?

entries.title: Between Rooms · Constellation Atlas of 89 public project doors
entries.summary: A dated public Git map snapshot with 89 repository addresses, 34 explicitly scoped role notes, five source-declared relations and six candidate compositions including GHoT energy-aware compute, LOADOUT, GRAFT, and accountable institutional invitations. The static atlas does not execute projects or establish partner/canon status.
entries.reviewQuestion: Which single source-owned capability, exact version, willing local steward and destination reviewer should be independently authorized for one bounded crossing?

entries.title: The Missing Handoff — public Waseca food supply need
entries.summary: October 2026 Waseca sources show rising food shelf sourcing pressure, welcomed donated produce and existing Waseca co-op/MSU study of food rescue logistics. webZ now contains a source-backed, no-client-data fictional handoff demonstration. No specific recipient-defined software bottleneck, partners, field work, or verified deliveries exist.
entries.reviewQuestion: Ask one authorized food shelf steward which sourcing or receiving coordination step actually needs improvement, and check with co-op/MSU teams for prior work; HOLD without their answers.

entries.title: The Suitcase Internet — portable signed offline room handoff
entries.summary: SUITCASE-001 is a browser-based offline-shell demonstration: distinct devices can create nonexportable P-256 keys, exchange signed public-safe offers and separate HOLD/REFUSE/REVIEW files. Six church, campus and community node patterns are unapproved proposals. No encrypted payloads, real-world identity checks, native reLATTE relay, enrolled hosts or field outcomes.
entries.reviewQuestion: Verify a fictional signed request and independent refusal across two offline devices, then ask ONE willing physical host steward for permission to review safeguarding, power and data policies.
